newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Feb 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Feb 7.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

Today detectives announced that the "Avon Lady' who apparently killed a knife attacker in a struggle at her home, will not be charged with any offence. Police decided not to charge Mrs Hertz after it was disclosed that David Stuchbery had conducted a similar attack 30 years previously.
C&W AND VEBA PULL PLUG ON GERMAN LINK

Cable & Wireless has broken up its two years standing telecoms alliance with German industrial group Veba. The company claimed there was a "difference in priorities' between the two groups. The break-up of the alliance seems set to result in a reshuffle of global telecoms alliances.
ANITE HOLDERS STORM AT ONE STG SALE TO EX-BOSS
Former Cray Electronics, now known as Anite is set for a difficult time today at an extraordinary meeting over the sale of a subsidiary to a former chairman of the company for just one stg.
UK POWER GROUP AIMS FOR 450 MLN STG IN AUSSIE BOND ISSUE
National Power has announced a 900 million Australian dollar (450 million stg) bond and paper raising exercise on the Australian debt for funding. The company is the first offshore company to do so.
DOCKLANDS BOMB BLAST COST PASSES 150 MLN STG MARK
The estimated cost of the damage incurred in last year's IRA bomb in South Quay docklands is estimated above 150 million stg.
UNDER THE COSH OSHKOSH CLOSES DOWN IN OSHKOSH
Oshkosh B'Gosh has announced that it is to shed 75 workers with the closure of its hometown Oshkosh, Wisconsin plant.
